title: Repealed provision
note: Repealed by the Workmen's Breach of Contract (Repealing) Act, 1925 (Act 3 of 1925), section 2 and Schedule. Retained here for historical numbering only. Do not treat it as an operative offence or assign BNS 357 to it.

title: Breach of contract to attend on and supply wants of helpless person
note: A lawful contract must bind the accused to attend on a person or supply that person's wants. The person must, because of youth, unsoundness of mind, disease or bodily weakness, be helpless or incapable of providing for their own safety or supplying their own wants. The accused must voluntarily omit the contracted attendance or supply. BNS 357 retains this structure: imprisonment of either description up to three months, or fine up to Rs 5,000, or both. The historical central IPC 491 maximum fine was Rs 200, with the same three-month imprisonment ceiling. The text does not make actual injury or death an additional ingredient.

title: Repealed provision
note: Also repealed by the Workmen's Breach of Contract (Repealing) Act, 1925, section 2 and Schedule. This entry preserves continuity with the supplied IPC chapter. It does not create a current criminal remedy for an ordinary employment or service-contract breach.
